headline: Oil posts second weekly drop as supply surplus outweighs Hormuz mine reports
summary: The stories that stayed in the briefing most this week: Oil posts second weekly drop as supply surplus outweighs Hormuz mine reports; Democrats hold Kansas governorship; Trump praises Mississippi winner Colom; Ontario plans OSAP caps and online-program ban for private career colleges.

top.headline: Oil posts second weekly drop as supply surplus outweighs Hormuz mine reports
top.what: Brent crude ended Friday little changed near US$96 a barrel and lost about 2.5% on the week, its second straight weekly decline, as forecasts of a growing supply surplus offset President Trump's decision to keep the blockade on Iran. Iran reported more tankers hitting mines near the Strait of Hormuz, and the United Nations nuclear agency said it cannot confirm that no nuclear material in Iran has been diverted.
top.why: In the briefing on 6 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Democrats hold Kansas governorship; Trump praises Mississippi winner Colom
top.what: The Associated Press on Thursday declared Democrat Cindy Holscher the winner of the Kansas governor's race, nine days after the vote, and Republican Ty Masterson conceded. President Trump praised Democrat Scott Colom, who won Mississippi's Senate seat a day earlier.
top.why: In the briefing on 6 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Ontario plans OSAP caps and online-program ban for private career colleges
top.what: Colleges Minister Nolan Quinn on Thursday outlined legislation that would limit how fast OSAP-funded enrolment can grow at private career colleges and cut off student aid for programs taught mainly online. The bill is expected to be tabled Monday.
top.why: In the briefing on 5 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Canada's U.S. envoy warns tariffs are raising costs and chilling investment
top.what: Ambassador Mark Wiseman said tariff uncertainty is pushing up costs and discouraging business expansion, a day after Carney said the Trump administration remains Canada's main negotiating partner.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Immigration minister hits back after Poilievre calls budget plan 'bonkers'
top.what: Immigration Minister Lena Diab on Thursday defended the immigration measures in last week's federal budget as temporary and aimed at people already in Canada, after Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre attacked the plan in a video.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Absent Democrats let Hegseth impeachment die; House GOP picks Jim Jordan as leader
top.what: Eleven Democrats missed Tuesday's 211-204 vote that shelved impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, enough to have changed the result, and House Republicans chose Jim Jordan to lead them in the minority.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Carney lands in Manila seeking trade deals with the Philippines and Southeast Asia
top.what: Prime Minister Mark Carney arrived in the Philippines early Saturday local time, where he is to meet President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and hopes to conclude trade agreements with that country and with the wider Southeast Asian bloc. He goes on to Cambodia and then China, where he plans to raise foreign interference with President Xi Jinping.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: EU leaders in Dublin fail to settle who speaks for Europe in Ukraine talks
top.what: A day after Ukraine and U.S. envoys said Europe would join the next round of peace talks with Russia, European Union leaders meeting in Dublin on Friday had not agreed on who should represent them. Names in play include European Council President António Costa, foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas and Finland's President Alexander Stubb.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.
